chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Salamah ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn al-Laith from Jabir ibn Isma'il from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him): A man asked the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) about the reward of standing in prayer at night with the Quran.

He said to him: Receive glad tidings. One who prays during one-tenth of the night for Allah, sincerely seeking His reward, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His angels: 'Record for this servant of Mine from the good deeds the number of all that Allah has caused to grow in the night, of its seeds, leaves, trees, and the number of every stalk, enclosure, and pasture.'
And one who prays for one-ninth of the night, Allah grants him ten accepted supplications and gives him his book in his right hand on the Day of Resurrection.
And one who prays for one-eighth of the night, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, grants him the reward of a patient martyr with sincere intention, and he is interceded for regarding his family.

And one who prays for one-seventh of the night, he emerges from his grave on the day he is raised with his face like the moon on the night of the full moon, until he passes over the Sirat (Bridge) with the secure ones.
And one who prays for one-sixth of the night, he is recorded among the repentant, and his past sins and future sins are forgiven.
And one who prays for one-fifth of the night, he jostles Abraham, the Friend of Allah, in his tent.
And one who prays for one-fourth of the night, he is among the first of the successful, until he passes over the Sirat like a fierce wind and enters Paradise without reckoning.

And one who prays for one-third of the night, no angel meets him except that he envies him for his station with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is said to him: Enter through whichever of the eight doors of Paradise you wish.

And one who prays for half the night, even if he were given the earth filled with gold seventy thousand times, his reward would not be equal to it; and for that, he is better than freeing seventy slaves from the progeny of Ismail.
And one who prays for two-thirds of the night, he has from the good deeds the amount of the sand of 'Araj; the smallest of them is heavier than Mount Uhud ten times over.

And one who prays a complete night, reciting the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, his remembrance being in bowing, prostrating, and remembering, is given from the reward its minimum being that he emerges from sins as his mother bore him, and it is recorded for him the number of all that Allah created of good deeds, and equal to them are ranks.

And light is established for him in his grave, and guilt and envy are removed from his heart, and he is protected from the punishment of the grave, and he is given a certificate of freedom from the Fire, and he is raised among the secure ones.
And the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels: 'O My angels! Look at My servant; he spent his night seeking My pleasure. Give him residence in Al-Firdaws.'

And for him in it are a hundred thousand cities; in each city is all that the souls desire and the eyes delight in, and what does not cross the mind, except what I have prepared for him of honor, increase, and proximity.

key_terms.صِرَاط: The Bridge over Hell on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.قِیَامُ اللَّیْلِ: Night prayer / Standing in prayer at night

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for praying different fractions of the night in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Saduq from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, this hadith outlines a graduated scale of rewards for Qiyam al-Layl, linking specific fractions of the night to distinct spiritual merits such as forgiveness, intercession for one's family, and the purification of the heart from envy. It highlights the Shia emphasis on the transformative power of night worship, culminating in the reward for a full night of prayer, which grants direct entry to Al-Firdaws and divine pleasure, surpassing the merit of freeing seventy slaves. This tradition underscores the concept of 'Ikhlas' (sincerity) as the primary condition for receiving these multiplied rewards, reflecting the broader Shia theological focus on the night as a time of intimate communion with God.
